checks.what: Tang vassal_start 647 on the 1,278 Transbaikal cells (Chita, Buryatia) that the Clio Tang 647 shape draws. Page: Yanran established 647, its territory 'extended from Lake Baikal to the north ... the Greater Khingan to the east'; 'It controlled the Mongolian Plateau from 647 to 682'. Cells (99-120 E, 49.2-52.8 N) lie inside that extent. Stage: the 1,278 cells carry the vassal tint 647-681 (were direct Tang); mirrors the dossier's own 647 event.
Tang vassal_end 682 on the same cells; page 'from 647 to 682'. The Tang 682 keyframe drops the cells anyway; stage shows them gone from Tang in 682, nothing left behind.

Restoration movement loses Baekje (core) minus Juryu to the Ungjin Commandery in 662. Battle of Baekgang page: by 662 'their area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity'; Juryu 'in modern Seocheon County, South Chungcheong'. Gunsan 30 km resolves to 8 cells (126.63-126.96 E, 35.75-36.23 N), straddling the Geum estuary and covering Seocheon; the gazetteer has no Seocheon. Same counterpart as the dossier's skipped ledger/1. Stage: 152 cells to Ungjin (Tang vassal) in 662, 8 stay with the movement.

Ungjin Commandery gains Juryu (Gunsan 30 km, 8 cells) in October 663. Baekgang page: battle 27-28 August 663 lunar (4-5 October Julian), the movement crushed, Juryu's captor undated; Ungjin page: 'existed between 660 and 671', 'created in place of Baekje in present-day Chungcheong Province' (Seocheon is in South Chungcheong). Stage: Baekje core is Ungjin 663-670 instead of ownerless (pub: 160 cells neutral 663-669), Silla 671. Note: the dossier's own skipped ledger/2 and successor give Juryu to Silla (Baekgang page: Churyu was under Silla siege in 663); the patch picks Ungjin without saying so. 8 cells, 64 cell-years; either reading fits the pages.

Tang gains Inner Mongolia from the eastern Gokturks in 645. Eastern Turkic Khaganate infobox: 'Buffer state of the Tang dynasty (639-645)', 'Reconquest by Tang dynasty: 645'. Same region as the dossier's own 630 vassal_start and 645 vassal_end. Stage: 4,431 ex-vassal cells are direct Tang 645-646 (pub: neutral); Khitan and Xueyantuo cells untouched. Note: this makes a two-year direct-Tang band between the vassal tint of 630-644 and 647+; the page also has the Xueyantuo push the Ashina south of the river in 642, which the draft does not draw (not this patch's doing).

Alamannia gains Swabia from the Franks in 644. Alamannia page: after Dagobert's death the duchy 'broke its ties with its Frankish sovereigns and struggled for independence', 'largely successful until the early 8th century'; territory centred on Lake Constance, upper Danube to the Lech, High Rhine, Black Forest. The spec (Clio 'Frisia Kingdom' 644, a mislabelled Swabia shape, 7.35-11.06 E, 46.9-50.5 N) is the same outline as the Alamannia dossier's own 496-723 and 724 keyframes; it resolves to 239 cells (note says 241). Stage: 179 cells to Alamannia 644-699 (pub: neutral); the other 60 stay with Austrasia. Year 644 is the Frankish dossier's (page: break after 638/639), consistent with the Frankish keyframes.

tang-dynasty_633: dossier correction kept unchanged (inner minus identical to the dossier's), Chita and Buryatia cut. Page: bridle prefectures from 629/630 around the southern Ordos; Xueyantuo until 645-646; plateau controlled 'from 647 to 682'. Stage: 1,278 Transbaikal cells no longer direct Tang 633-646 (snap 633 adds 490, was 1,768).
tang-dynasty_638: same cut as 633 on the dossier's unchanged correction; supported as above.
tang-dynasty_641: same cut on the dossier's unchanged correction; Transbaikal not Tang 641-646; supported as above.

tang-dynasty_618 (618-622): dossier core plus the region of the dossier's own ledger/1 (identical spec). Emperor Gaozu page: 'In winter 617, he captured Chang'an'; 'Li Xiaogong was able to persuade the Sui cities in modern southern Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Chongqing to submit'; 'In spring 618, Emperor Yang was killed'; reign from 18 June 618. Stage: the 1,472 Sichuan/Chongqing/Hanzhong cells are Tang 618-622 (pub: neutral until 623); snap removes 392 instead of 1,859.

eastern-roman-empire_617: Egypt no longer subtracted. Page: invasion began 'either in 617 or 618'; 'Alexandria was then betrayed to the Persians by a certain Peter in June 619'; 'by 621, the province was securely in Persian hands'; nothing Persian in Egypt in 617-618. Stage: Egypt Roman 617-618 (pub: 2,008 cells ownerless 617-622), Alexandria Persian 619, the rest Persian 621.

umayyad-caliphate_692: dossier correction kept, Algeria cut. Maghreb page: Kairouan retaken 688/9; nothing Arab-held in Algeria before 700 (Abu al-Muhajir only raided to Milev and Tlemcen); Hippo Regius falls 'soon after' the Kahina's death 'around 701'; Zab (Numidia) first a province in 705; west taken 708-709. Stage 692: Algeria Exarchate 436, Altava 173, Byzantine 47, rest ownerless (pub: Umayyad 3,281, Altava 1).
umayyad-caliphate_693: dossier correction kept, Algeria cut; supported as for 692.
umayyad-caliphate_694 (694-697): dossier correction kept, Algeria cut; supported as for 692. Stage 697: Exarchate's 436 Algerian cells contested with the caliphate, Altava 173.

umayyad-caliphate_698 (698-700): dossier correction kept, Algeria cut. Page: Carthage taken, 'ending the Byzantine presence by 698'; Kahina defeated around 701; 'Similarly unknown is the fate of the Algerian coastal cities'. Stage 698-699: Aures 702, Altava 173, Byzantine 21; the Exarchate's 436 coastal cells ownerless after 698 (pub: Umayyad), which the page leaves open. Span reaches 700 (next window).

baekje-restoration-movement_662 (662-663): Gunsan 30 km (8 cells) in place of the unresolvable 'Seocheon 30 km'. Baekgang page: Juryu 'in modern Seocheon County'; control 'confined to the fortress of Churyu and its immediate vicinity' by 662. The disc covers Seocheon across the Geum estuary.

Rashidun over Byzantium 656-660 in Libya. The page backs Cyrenaica ('Barqa fell without opposition'; Uqba left as 'Governor of Barqa'; lost only in 690) but not Tripolitania: Tripoli 'had fallen back into the hands of the Byzantines soon after Amr ibn al-Aas' departure' (at 647). The why quoted only 'fell in around 643' and the region was all of Libya. The ruling settled only the 378 Cyrenaica cells (all inside the 'Cyrenaica' region), so the effect was right but the scope was wider than the page.
checks.fix: Region narrowed from country Libya to region Cyrenaica and why corrected (Tripoli's return to Byzantium noted, 378 cells). Re-checked: --check-patch ok; trial still settles 378 cell-years in 1 year; Cyrenaica Rashidun 656-660.

checks.what: Umayyad over Byzantium 661-689 in Libya. Settles Cyrenaica 661 (378 cells) and 163 Tripolitanian cells in 666 (Byzantine 666-679 in pub, Umayyad in stage). The why described the 163 cells as 'Surt, Misratah', but they run 11.5-18.8 E, Tripoli and the coast to the Tunisian border included, and it did not cite the page's support for Tripoli: in 666/7 raids went 'via Tripoli - now emerging as a centre for Muslim naval forces' while 'Uqba ibn Nafi was campaigning in Sirte, Fezzan'. Effect supported.
checks.fix: Why corrected to describe the cells settled and to quote the page's 666/7 Tripoli sentence; region and years unchanged. Re-checked: --check-patch ok; trial still settles 541 cell-years in 2 years.
